pr_title: Clarify which files can use hard links during first-run setup
pr_body:
* Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/21904
  * Maybe this needs to be rebased on #21886 to avoid merge conflicts. Can do if and/or when that's preferred.
pr_comments: This is too much. Please open a new pull request that only adds support for a `Songs` folder not at the normal location.

issue_context.title: Hard link creation flow does not consider users changing `BeatmapDirectory` in stable
issue_context.body:
This check is not completely correct for beatmaps: https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/ea8beffa612016460a7df64736c7d9dbe61fd4f8/osu.Game/Database/LegacyImportManager.cs#L64-L67 For beatmaps, I believe it should be checking via `stableStorage.GetSongStorage()` specifically, as that is not the same and can in particular lead to a different drive. ### Discussed in https://github.com/ppy/osu/discussions/21902
Originally posted by **hrfarmer** December 28, 2022 So I have my stable installation on my C drive, but in the .ini file I changed my songs folder to be on my D drive. Whenever I tried to import my maps in the setup wizard (with lazer being on my C drive as well), it still started duplicating all my beatmaps, which I cannot do because I will run out of storage. For now I'm just moving stable over to my D drive so I can do the hard link there, but I'm wondering if there is a fix for this.
comments: @LittleEndu can you confirm that you're taking this one on? else i'll add it to my list.

I can try again taking into account what bdach and frenzy discussed with me, but your final comment in the PR left me confused. 

Lazer will already try to make hard links when possible, and would do so even if stable uses custom Songs directory. The issue here is that it's not made clear to the user during first-run setup, the message is flat out wrong most of the time.

The change that needs to be made is that the display on the first run setup should take into account the final location of the `Songs` folder, which it doesn't right now seemingly. This was already in your PR as far as I could tell.

Scores / replays / skins can be ignored as they are relatively a small amount of data compared to beatmaps.

Does that make things clearer?

review_comments: Why is _this entire logic_ if-else'd and copypasted rather than the retrieval of `testExistingPath` alone?

I did this to handle `StableContent.All` or checking a combination of different flags. So should this function only allow checking either beatmaps or others and not both at same time? Can probably use bool then instead of `StableContent`.

That's missing the forest for the trees. `StableContent` is nowhere as much of an issue as trying to explain to the user all of the minute complications of them having shipped off part of their files to another drive and what that means for hard link migration.

The enum was just one part of it focusing on the unnecessary use of the if conditionals, as I've also proposed a better method of checking availability without basically duplicating code (use of local methods).
Can we not split hairs like this? Can we just stick to all-or-nothing on this? Not only is this difficult for us to maintain, people will have no idea what they're being told here.
Sure, but then #21904 has no reason to remain open...

Seeing the complexity associated with hypercorrect handling of this I say we just check both paths for hard link availability and tell the user their data is gonna get copied unless they move everything on one drive.
So change first if to `if (beatmapsAvailable && othersAvailable)` and keep everything else as is in master?
That's what I'd do. Dunno. Need more opinions. I thought this was initially going to be simpler to support well but hadn't considered the complexity behind it.

Agree with making sure both the stable folder and the beatmaps folder are in the same drive as the lazer folder. Having one side of lazer data storage copied from stable while the other being linked feels bad, as opposed to requesting the user to just change their installation location to the same drive.

This isn't what's happening here nor anywhere else, this here is only changing the explanation text. Hard links will be used with any imported file where hard linking succeeds via `TryCreateHardLink`. Lazer storage will always be in good state because hard links have to be in the same drive where lazer storage is and every other file will fail to create hard link and be copied instead. As such I don't see copying some files while hard linking other as an issue.

The point is that *we don't want to be showing complex explanations to the user*, because the more complicated they are, the less likely it is that they'll understand. *At most* I'd agree to a message saying "your beatmaps are on another drive than the rest of the files, so we can't hard link everything" and leave the rest for them to figure out, rather than going into painstaking detail about what is where.

Should there be three explanations then? The current ones where either all or none of the files can use hard links, and a new one when stable uses a `BeatmapDirectory` which makes it impossible to hard link all files. The third explanation could then just be that - "Your previous osu! install stores files in multiple drives. Data migration can't make use of hard links for all of them." and then maybe link them to https://osu.ppy.sh/wiki/en/Client/Program_files/User_configuration_file#not-changeable-in-game wiki page in addition to the lazer hard link one??

People who are going to manually edit their .cfg files are a minority anyway. I agree that they can figure out what's going to get hard linked vs what isn't.
Not sure linking the wiki page adds anything to the message, such users should be well aware of it. Otherwise this reads pretty clear to me.
My only concern is that changing the `BeatmapDirectory` is a set and forget kinda deal and users might need a reminder of where their beatmaps are stored.
